#!/usr/bin/env python3
import asyncio
import json
import os
from pyppeteer import launch

async def scrape_prices():
    browser = await launch(
        headless=False,
        args=['--no-sandbox']
    )

    page = await browser.newPage()
    await page.goto('http://localhost:8080/products')

    await page.waitForSelector('.product', timeout=5000)

    products = await page.evaluate('''() => {
        const items = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
        return Array.from(items).map(item => ({
            name: item.querySelector('.name').textContent,
            price: item.querySelector('.price').textContent
        }));
    }''')

    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    output_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'prices.json')

    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(products, f, indent=2)

    await browser.close()
    print(f"Scraped {len(products)} products to {output_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(scrape_prices())

Analysis: I can see the scrape.py script. The issue is that it has `headless=False` which means it's trying to launch chromium with a GUI, but this is a headless/IoT environment without a display. This will cause chromium to hang. The script also only has `--no-sandbox` flag. On minimal/IoT images, chromium typically needs additional flags to run properly in headless mode.
Plan: I'll: 1) Check if the test server is running on localhost:8080, 2) Modify the script to set headless=True and add additional chromium flags commonly needed for headless environments (--disable-dev-shm-usage, --disable-gpu, --disable-setuid-sandbox, --no-first-run, --no-zygote, --single-process), 3) Test the modified script.
